cases.title: Server under plain Node is unchanged
steps: npm run build -w graph-execution && npm run build -w graph-manager
Start the server as TESTING.md "graph-manager" describes, but with GM_PORT=0
Log in with curl and GET /api/health with the cookie
cases.expected: The console prints "graph-manager listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>" and /api/health answers 200 {"ok":true}

cases.title: Forked server reports its port over IPC
steps: Build graph-manager
In node, fork apps/graph-manager/dist/server/main.js with stdio ["ignore","pipe","pipe","ipc"] and env GM_PASSWORD=pw GM_PORT=0 GM_DATA_DIR/GM_WORKSPACES_DIR set to temp dirs
Wait for the first IPC message, then GET /healthz on that port
cases.expected: The message is {type:"listening", port:<n>} with n>0 and /healthz answers 200

cases.title: Terminal shim runs graph-execution
steps: Start the server as in P1 with GM_GRAPH_EXECUTION_BIN unset
POST /api/terminals with the cookie, open its WebSocket as apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/terminals.test.ts does
Send input "graph-execution --version\r"
cases.expected: The terminal output contains the version from packages/graph-execution/package.json, and <GM_DATA_DIR>/bin/graph-execution runs an absolute runtime path (not plain node)

cases.title: Root checks pass with the new workspace
steps: npm install
npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run build && npm test
cases.expected: All four commands exit 0, and the output includes the graph-manager-desktop test files

cases.title: Packaged app smoke test on macOS
steps: npm run dist -w graph-manager-desktop
npm run smoke -w graph-manager-desktop
cases.expected: release/ contains a .dmg and the smoke script prints "OK: desktop smoke passed" (server answers, cookie works, terminal echoes gm-smoke-ok, server and server.lock gone after quit)

cases.title: Dev app in smoke mode binds only to loopback
steps: Build all three workspaces

Run apps/graph-manager-desktop/node_modules/.bin/electron (or the root node_modules/.bin/electron) apps/graph-manager-desktop --user-data-dir=<tmp> with GM_DESKTOP_SMOKE=1 GM_DATA_DIR=<tmp>/gm-data GM_WORKSPACES_DIR=<tmp>/gm-ws (never let it use the real ~/.graph-manager)
Read <tmp>/smoke.json, then curl http://<this machine LAN IP>:<port>/healthz
Check <tmp>/gm-data/server.lock holds the smoke port
Touch <tmp>/smoke-quit
cases.expected: smoke.json has ok:true; server.lock holds the port; the LAN IP request fails to connect while 127.0.0.1 answers 200; the app exits after smoke-quit and server.lock is gone

cases.title: Local server refuses requests without the desktop cookie
steps: With the app running as in P6, GET http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/health with no cookie

cases.title: A fake run starts through the API under the bundled runtime
steps: With the app running as in P6, create a git repo under <tmp>/gm-ws/local/o/r with packages/graph-execution/src/__fixtures__/diamond copied in and committed (see TESTING.md for a temp repo)

POST /api/runs/<workspace id> with the cookie and {"tasksDir":"diamond","spec":"<fixture spec>","provider":"fake"} (read apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/runs.ts for the body and workspace id format)
cases.expected: Status 201 with runId and viewUrl, and the run reaches applied or done

cases.title: Second server on the same data folder refuses
steps: npm run build -w graph-execution && npm run build -w graph-manager
Start node apps/graph-manager/dist/server/main.js with GM_PASSWORD=pw GM_PORT=0 GM_DATA_DIR=<tmp>/data GM_WORKSPACES_DIR=<tmp>/ws GM_DOCKER_SOCKET=<tmp>/none.sock in the background and note its port
Check <tmp>/data/server.lock holds that pid and port
Start a second node apps/graph-manager/dist/server/main.js with GM_PORT=0 and the same GM_DATA_DIR=<tmp>/data GM_WORKSPACES_DIR=<tmp>/ws GM_DOCKER_SOCKET=<tmp>/none.sock
cases.expected: The second process prints "graph-manager is already running on this data folder (pid <first pid>, http://127.0.0.1:<first port>)" and exits with code 3; the first one still answers /healthz 200

cases.title: Stale lock does not block a start
steps: Build graph-manager
Write <tmp>/data/server.lock by hand with {"pid": <pid of a process that has exited>, "port": 1, "host": "127.0.0.1", "startedAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}
Start node apps/graph-manager/dist/server/main.js with GM_PASSWORD=pw GM_PORT=0 GM_DATA_DIR=<tmp>/data GM_WORKSPACES_DIR=<tmp>/ws GM_DOCKER_SOCKET=<tmp>/none.sock
cases.expected: The server starts and prints "graph-manager listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>"; server.lock now holds the new pid and port

cases.title: Port fallback only with GM_PORT_FALLBACK
steps: Build graph-manager
Hold a port P with node -e "require(\"net\").createServer().listen(P,\"127.0.0.1\")"
Start the server with GM_PASSWORD=pw GM_PORT=P GM_DATA_DIR=<tmp>/data GM_WORKSPACES_DIR=<tmp>/ws GM_DOCKER_SOCKET=<tmp>/none.sock
Stop it if it started, then start it with GM_PASSWORD=pw GM_PORT=P GM_PORT_FALLBACK=1 and a fresh GM_DATA_DIR=<tmp>/data GM_WORKSPACES_DIR=<tmp>/ws GM_DOCKER_SOCKET=<tmp>/none.sock
cases.expected: Without the variable it exits 1 with "port P is already in use: pass --port or set GM_PORT". With it, it prints "port P is in use, using <m>" and listens on m != P, /healthz answers 200

cases.title: IPC shutdown removes the lock
steps: Build graph-manager

In node, fork apps/graph-manager/dist/server/main.js with stdio ["ignore","pipe","pipe","ipc"] and env GM_PASSWORD=pw GM_PORT=0 GM_DATA_DIR=<tmp>/data GM_WORKSPACES_DIR=<tmp>/ws GM_DOCKER_SOCKET=<tmp>/none.sock
Wait for {type:"listening"}, then child.send({type:"shutdown"})
cases.expected: The child exits with code 0 within 10 s and <tmp>/data/server.lock no longer exists

cases.title: Desktop local server uses the shared data folder and its password
steps: npm run build
Run the desktop unit tests: npm test -w graph-manager-desktop
cases.expected: localServer tests pass: the forked server uses GM_DATA_DIR from the env, the login uses <dataDir>/password, AlreadyRunning is raised for a second start on the same folder, and stop() removes server.lock
